question: Which country has announced that only climbers who have previously summited a peak above 7,000 meters will be allowed to climb Everest?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Government of Nepal** has announced new eligibility rules for those attempting to climb **Mount Everest**.
 
• Under the revised policy, only climbers who have **successfully summited a peak above 7,000 meters** will be allowed to climb Everest.
 
• This move is aimed at improving safety standards and **reducing the number of inexperienced climbers** attempting the dangerous ascent.
 
• The decision comes in the wake of multiple deaths and overcrowding incidents witnessed during recent climbing seasons.
 
• Authorities are also looking to introduce stricter checks on climbers’ health and ensure **adequate insurance and trained support staff**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mount Everest**, standing at 8,848.86 meters, lies on the Nepal-Tibet border and is the world’s highest mountain.
 
• Nepal earns significant revenue through climbing permits, with each Everest permit costing around **USD 11,000**.
 
• In the 2023 spring season, Nepal issued a record number of over 460 Everest permits, leading to **dangerous overcrowding**.
 
• The recent change aligns with calls from international mountaineering bodies for **better regulation of high-altitude climbing**.
 
• Nepal is also working on improving **rescue infrastructure and weather forecasting systems** to prevent climbing disasters.
